clue.text: The fairy-tale drudge caught at home with the German girl

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
in means at home, as in 'staying in'
der is a German word for 'the'
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A storybook servant girl is found at home in the company of a German girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of the pantomime story is the ill-treated stepdaughter made to do all the household chores.

clue.text: In the same place a river rises in the Peninsula

parts.note: ib. is short for ibidem, Latin for 'in the same place', used in footnotes

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for the river is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A river climbs to its source somewhere on a peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns AIRE into ERIA. The definition is the Iberian Peninsula, home of Spain and Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: The landmass holding Spain and Portugal is known by this name, the Iberian Peninsula.

clue.text: Reject record with feeble sound

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: the word sound tells us to take how the word for feeble is pronounced, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a feeble excuse is a lame one

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a recording because its audio quality is weak.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or refuse to own something is to reject it.

clue.text: Appear again to receive writer's reward?

indicators.note: one word taking in another, as a hand receives a gift, puts the second inside the first

parts.note: to come back, or recome, is to appear again
a pen is a writer, and the possessive 's gives PENS

explanation.surface: Does an author who shows up again get paid for it?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful idea of a writer paid simply for turning up again; 'to receive' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensation given for effort or loss is a payment or prize earned.

clue.text: Drag swimmer up away from the wind

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means both pieces together are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to drag is to draw, as in pulling a cart
an eel is a swimming fish

explanation.surface: Hauling a fish upwards, out of the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DRAWEEL around as a whole, giving LEEWARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call the sheltered side, facing where the breeze is heading, the lee side.

clue.text: Some seafarers observed at a great distance

indicators.note: only some of the letters of seafarers are taken, a run from inside the word

explanation.surface: A few sailors were spotted far out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Far off or far away describes something very distant.

clue.text: Picture of a girl embraced by both parents

indicators.note: the girl is hugged, so placed inside, by the parents

parts.note: pa and ma are father and mother
pa and ma are father and mother
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A photo of a daughter being hugged by her mother and father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' pictures the parents hugging the girl, which is exactly how the letters sit: the girl in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide view or a broad survey is a sweeping scene or picture.

clue.text: Corrupt assignment involving, say, upheaval for Chateaubriand

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the date wraps round the other letters

parts.note: an assignation or date is an assignment to meet
e.g. means 'for example', so say

indicators.note: in a down clue, a heaving up means the name is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: François-René de Chateaubriand was a French writer, whose novel René bears his own name

explanation.surface: A dishonest arrangement involves some literary upheaval for the French author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheaval' turns RENE into ENER. Chateaubriand is also a steak, a tempting red herring; here it is the French writer, whose first name is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Degenerate as a verb means to deteriorate morally, which is to become corrupt.

clue.text: Deceptive appearance of accountant in decline

indicators.note: the accountant is placed in the middle of the word for decline

parts.note: to fade is to decline
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An accountant is putting on a brave front while going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: A building's front, used figuratively for a false outward show.

clue.text: Cell about right for minister's sentence

indicators.note: about means going round, so the cell surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: a vesicle is a small sac or cell in biology

explanation.surface: A prison cell is the right place for a clergyman's sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell' and 'sentence' suggest prison, but the cell is biological and the sentence is a line said in church.
explanation.definitionFit: In church services a short line said by the officiant, answered by the congregation, is a versicle.

clue.text: Replace tie with vestment from the cupboard

indicators.note: read as re-place, the word for tie is placed again the other way round

parts.note: a match that is a tie is a draw
a robe is a vestment

explanation.surface: Someone swaps a necktie for a clerical robe taken from the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replace' turns DRAW into WARD. 'tie' looks like a necktie but is a drawn game.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall cupboard for hanging clothes.

clue.text: Story of a gang-leader in South America

indicators.note: the article and the gang's leader go in the middle of the letters for South America
the leader of gang is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tale about the head of a criminal gang in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A long tale, originally a Norse heroic narrative.

clue.text: Diligence of a lecturer in theatre studies?

explanation.surface: How hard-working is a drama lecturer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diligence' looks like hard work, but a diligence is a French public coach. The second half reads the answer as a stage coach, a tutor of drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A diligence was a horse-drawn public carriage; a coach is also a tutor, here one for the theatre.

clue.text: Freely render a rash paper

indicators.note: freely means without restraint, so the letters are rearranged at will

explanation.surface: Translate an impetuous newspaper loosely.
explanation.walkthrough: To render a text is to express it in other words, which is what this answer does.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate a passage in other words is to render it in a new form.

clue.text: M.P.S with chair working

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held and printed as 'M.P.S with chair working': the anagram of MPS + CHAIR needs A and T to give the answer, and no clue word supplies them ('with' would have to read 'at', four letters off)

clue.text: Determined to place barrier between articles and books

indicators.note: the barrier is put between the two articles

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a is the indefinite article
a dam is a barrier across a river
NT is the New Testament, a group of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Resolved to put a barrier between his papers and his books.
explanation.definitionFit: Unyielding and resolute, firmly set on a course.

clue.text: Suitable for ploughing about mid-August? It's doubtful

indicators.note: about means going round, so the farmland word surrounds the middle letters

parts.note: arable land is land fit for ploughing

indicators.note: mid means the middle letters of August are taken

explanation.surface: Is the land fit to plough in late summer? Debatable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-' takes the middle two letters of August, GU. The surface suggests harvest-time farming, but 'Suitable for ploughing' is just a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Open to argument or dispute, hence uncertain or questionable.

clue.text: Wine, having taint, sad to say, is rejected

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or taint

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: alas expresses regret, so sad to say

explanation.surface: A wine with an off taste is, sadly, sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified dessert wine from Sicily.

clue.text: She suppressed Regan's initial desire to be like Katharina

indicators.note: suppressed means held down inside, so the letter goes inside she
initial means the first letter of Regan's is taken

parts.note: a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: A woman stifled the first impulse of a Shakespeare daughter to turn into another heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Regan is a daughter in King Lear, leading toward tragedy; Katharina is the heroine of The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Katharina is the bad-tempered, scolding heroine of a Shakespeare comedy about a nagging woman.

clue.text: Long exotic snake outside Italian city

indicators.note: the snake goes outside, round, the rearranged letters

parts.note: a boa is a large snake

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so the letters are made unfamiliar by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A long foreign snake lies outside an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' makes LOGN from LONG. 'Long' looks like a description of the snake, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The university city in northern Italy, capital of Emilia-Romagna.

clue.text: One more gin sling — a source of power for sailors

definitions.text: a source of power for sailors

indicators.note: a gin sling is a cocktail, but to sling is to throw about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Another gin cocktail: just what gives sailors their energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sling' looks like the gin cocktail but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The compartment of a ship housing its motors drives the vessel.

clue.text: Harrow's Lothario, perhaps

explanation.surface: The womanizer from the famous school.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public school, which tempts one to read this as a pupil; here the harrow is a farm tool and 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrow is a toothed tool that breaks up soil, much as a garden tool does; a Lothario is a womanizer or libertine.

clue.text: Novel about old Japanese garment

parts.note: Kim is a novel by Rudyard Kipling
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A novel about an old Japanese robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose wide-sleeved robe traditionally worn in Japan.

clue.text: Speech mostly about an alternative to the Messiah, say

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shortened speech surrounds the alternative
mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Most of a talk concerns something other than the Messiah, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' leaves ORATIO. 'Speech' leads toward a talk or address, and 'the Messiah' toward religion, but the definition is Handel's choral work as an example of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel's Messiah is a famous example of a large sacred choral work.

clue.text: One of three kings lacking a way to be prosperous

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letters for a way are removed

parts.note: there were three English kings named Richard
A plus RD, the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: One of the Magi without a path to wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three kings' suggests the Magi; it means the three English kings called Richard.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy or well-off, having plenty of money.

clue.text: Supporter grating on club? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: the clue says grating on, so after, club, but the opposite order puts the grating first

parts.note: a grid is a grating
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A fan grates on the nerves of the club, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' looks like a fan; it is a frame that supports, such as a grill over a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A framework of bars holding meat over a fire, or ships in dock, bears the weight.

clue.text: Football team's language!

explanation.surface: What do football fans speak?
explanation.walkthrough: Celtic is a Glasgow football club; the same word names the Gaelic and Brythonic group of languages.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish football club and the family of languages including Welsh and Gaelic share the name.

clue.text: Beat this as an object of infatuation!

definitions.text: Beat this as an object of infatuation!

parts.words: Beat this as an object of infatuation!
parts.note: a pulse of the chest's pumping organ, read also as the idol who makes that organ race

explanation.surface: A challenge to top somebody's crush.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive celebrity adored by fans makes their pulses quicken.
